title: Outboard Flap Track Fairing Attachment Rib — Cracking Repair

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

ata.title: Wings — Trailing Edge — Flap Track Support

abstract: Permanent repair for cracking of the outboard flap track fairing attachment rib, with the load path check that has to be made when the carriage roller set has been changed to the softer surface standard.

sections.purpose: To give the permanent repair for cracking found in the outboard flap track fairing attachment rib, and to define when the repair must be re-assessed because of a change at the carriage.
sections.damage_assessment: Cracking at the attachment rib starts at the forward fastener group and runs aft into the web. It is found during the flap track wear measurement, with the flap extended, and is normally associated with a carriage that has been running with excessive side play. Assess the crack with the flap extended and supported and the fairing removed. Measure the crack length from the fastener hole edge. Record the carriage side play at the same visit, because a crack in this rib on an aircraft with side play at the limit is a symptom rather than a finding in its own right. On aircraft where the carriage roller set has been changed to the softer surface standard, the load into the rib is slightly higher at the same side play, and the shorter of the two crack limits applies.
sections.repair_procedure: Extend the flap and support it on the trestle. Remove the track fairing. Clean the rib and remove the paint over the forward fastener group. Do the eddy current inspection over the whole forward group and mark every indication. Stop-drill the crack at its tip and deburr both faces. Cut the repair angle from the material listed and form it to the rib radius. Position it so that it picks up the two existing fastener rows and gives a 20 mm minimum edge margin at the free edge. Drill the new pattern through into the rib, using the drill jig on the drawing so that the new holes clear the internal radius. Do an eddy current inspection at every new hole before any fastener is installed. Install the angle D5730118419315 wet with sealant and fasten it with the bolts EN441172-29 at the structural rows. Install the doubler D5730124726204 over the aft end of the angle where the crack has entered the web. Re-protect the whole repaired area and re-apply the paint scheme. Install the track fairing and check the clearance to the carriage through the full flap travel.
sections.inspection_requirements: Do an eddy current inspection over the repair at completion and record the baseline. Repeat it at every flap track wear measurement, and in any case at every 4 000 flight cycles. Record the carriage side play at every repeat inspection; if the play has increased since the repair, the carriage must be dealt with before the repair is cleared again. A crack that reappears outside the repair footprint invalidates this scheme.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: A single crack up to 30 mm long from a fastener hole in the forward group on aircraft with the delivered roller set, or up to 22 mm on aircraft with the softer surface roller set. No crack that reaches the rib to spar attachment is repairable under this scheme.

repair_drawings.title: Repair angle and web doubler, outboard flap track fairing attachment rib

type_data.fastener_pattern: Two structural rows of 13 shear bolts at 24 mm pitch with 20 mm edge distance, drilled through the jig so that the new holes clear the internal rib radius by at least 6 mm.
type_data.fatigue_life_note: Repair is life-limited to 16 000 flight cycles, with a repeat eddy current inspection every 4 000 flight cycles and at every flap track wear measurement.
